nodes.label: Frame 04701 - Daylight Broiler House Overhead (IPC-Gas, 2022-02-23 11:04:26)
nodes.description: Color overhead CCTV still of a commercial broiler house floor. A horizontal suspended feed line runs left-to-right across the mid-frame carrying five white pan feeders with red central cones. Several hundred small white broilers (early growth stage, small body footprint) are densely packed, with a large amorphous aggregation blob in the upper-centre and tight rosettes of birds ringing each feeder pan. Litter floor is visible and bare in the lower third. OSD burn-in: camera name '1080P-IPC-Gas' top-left, timestamp top-right.
nodes.rationale: Serves as a training-split exemplar of the daylight, high-contrast, colour imaging regime with clear bird/litter separation - the easiest condition for a detector and therefore the implicit visual baseline the harder night/IR frames are compared against.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Gas Camera Viewpoint
nodes.description: One of two named fixed IP-camera installations whose identifier is burned into the top-left OSD as '1080P-IPC-Gas'. It observes a broiler pen with the same five-pan suspended feed-line layout as the Siren camera but from a slightly flatter, less distorted angle.
nodes.rationale: The 'Gas' suffix most plausibly names the environmental stimulus or zone the camera monitors rather than the camera hardware, which would make the camera identifier a proxy for experimental condition.

nodes.label: Suspended Five-Pan Feed Line Rig
nodes.description: The rigid horizontal pipe carrying five evenly spaced circular pan feeders (white lattice pan, red central delivery cone) that crosses every frame at roughly the same height. It is the only geometrically stable, high-contrast structure in the scene across all lighting conditions and both cameras.
nodes.rationale: Its invariance makes it the natural spatial reference for registering frames, defining feeder-proximity zones for behaviour scoring, and estimating the lens distortion field.

nodes.label: Fixed Overhead Surveillance Framing
nodes.description: The shared acquisition geometry of the dataset: a ceiling-mounted static camera looking down at a shallow oblique angle onto the litter floor, producing top-down teardrop-shaped bird silhouettes with minimal side profile and no camera motion between frames.
nodes.rationale: A static overhead rig means background subtraction and fixed region-of-interest masks remain valid across the whole corpus, but it also means birds are only ever seen from one pose family, limiting what a detector can learn about body orientation.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera-Name OSD Overlay
nodes.description: Every frame carries DVR on-screen-display text rendered directly into the pixel data: the camera identifier in the top-left corner and an ISO-style 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' timestamp in the top-right corner.
nodes.rationale: The overlay supplies free per-frame acquisition metadata that would otherwise be lost when video is decomposed into stills, but because it is pixel-level rather than sidecar metadata it also occupies image area a convolutional model will see and can memorise.

nodes.label: Feeder-Centric Flock Aggregation
nodes.description: The recurring spatial signature in which birds form tight radial rosettes around each pan feeder, heads inward, producing local density far above the pen average while intervening litter stays comparatively bare.
nodes.rationale: Feeder rings are the highest-information region for welfare inference - occupancy around the pans tracks feeding motivation and competition - but they are also where mutual occlusion is worst, so the most behaviourally meaningful pixels are the hardest ones to segment.

hyperedges.label: Shared Fixed Broiler-House Scene Geometry Across All Frames
